newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine communists call for intensified war.
newsitem.headline: Philippine communists call for intensified war.

text.p: The Philippine Communist Party leadership has urged its fighters to intensify guerrilla warfare hand-in-hand with peace negotiations with the Manila government, a former armed forces chief said on Monday.

Retired army general and former senator Rodolfo Biazon said in media statement that party chief Armando Liwanag issued the call in a message on March 29 to the party's armed wing, the New People's Army (NPA) and posted on the Internet.
The military believes Armando Liwanag is a nom-de-guerre of party founder Jose Maria Sison, a chief rebel consultant in talks between Manila and the communist-led National Democratic Front (NDF).
The front maintains offices in the Netherlands, where most of the country's top communist leaders live in exile.
Biazon, as a former military chief and also a former member of the senate defence committee, periodically makes statements or observations regarding the insurgency situation.
He said the message called on NPA rebels "to intensify guerrilla warfare on a wide scale."
Liwanag ordered them to specifically target "notorious" human rights violators, anti-communist militia groups, rebel defectors, informers and "elements with blood debts to the people," Biazon said.
Leftist leader and former NDF officer Satur Ocampo confirmed there was such a directive from the NDF international offices, but said it was not a "specific battle order."

"They were general guidelines in the annual message of the chairman of the party reiterating and updating established policies in the light of developments in the revolutionary movement," Ocampo said.
He said he saw no conflict in the message and in the party's stance to hold peace negotiations with Manila.
The government and the NDF have held several rounds of talks in the Netherlands on ending an insurgency that has claimed more than 40,000 lives since 1969.
